intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Construction on NOvA's two massive neutrino detectors began in 2009.

intervals.label: first long-distance neutrinos
intervals.quote: saw its first long-distance neutrinos in November 2013

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Start is the first day of the neutrino-mode data set used in the NOvA 2022 oscillation analysis; the detector was still being filled at that time. END ADDED 2026-10-25 (mirrors experiment:nova): NuMI has had no beam since July 2024 ("The MI has not operated since July 2024", Fermilab PAC, April 2026 meeting). Previously open-ended.
intervals.quote: 13.6×10²⁰ POT from 555.3 s of integrated beam-pulse time recorded between February 6, 2014, to March 20, 2020

intervals.label: no NuMI beam (Main Injector transformer failures)
intervals.note: Derived from the beam source, as for experiment:nova: NuMI has had no beam since July 2024 and the restart is only planned (Sept 2026 PAC: stable beam planned for 1 October 2026; no later source confirms it). CONFLICTING STATEMENT (left unresolved, status kept): Fermilab's 7 July 2026 feature says NOvA 'is the only currently operating long-baseline neutrino experiment in the United States' and 'is taking data' (https://news.fnal.gov/2026/07/fermilab-marks-70-years-of-neutrino-science-and-leads-next-generation-experiment/); the PAC reports (April and September 2026) are more specific that the Main Injector has not delivered NuMI beam since July 2024, and the feature does not say which data. Shutdown here means no NuMI beam data-taking, not that the detectors are powered down.
intervals.quote: The MI has not operated since July 2024

placements.note: The detector saw its first long-distance neutrinos in November 2013 while still under construction; the placement start is the completion of construction in September 2014.
placements.quote: In September, the Department of Energy officially proclaimed construction of the experiment completed, on schedule and under budget.

baseline.quote: the 14 kt Far Detector (FD) is located on the surface, 810 km from the target, near Ash River, Minnesota

length.quote: It is a segmented tracking calorimeter, of dimensions 15.5 m×15.5 m×59.8 m, with 896 planes of 384 PVC cells.

off_axis_angle.quote: Both detectors are centered 14.6 mrad off the beam axis and receive a narrow-band neutrino flux peaked at 1.8 GeV.

overburden.note: The 2020 NOvA multimessenger paper gives 3 m.w.e. (1.3 m concrete + 16 cm barite).
overburden.quote: Shielded only by a 3.6 m water equivalent overburden, the FD is exposed to a cosmic-ray flux of 150 kHz.

total_mass.note: NOvA's own page says "a 14 metric-kiloton far detector in Minnesota just south of the U.S.-Canada border".
total_mass.quote: The 14 k Far Detector (FD) is located at Ash River, Minnesota, ∼810 km from the source.

description.quote: The detectors are made up of 344,000 cells of extruded, highly reflective plastic PVC filled with liquid scintillator.
description.value: 344,000 cells of extruded, highly reflective plastic PVC filled with liquid scintillator (both NOvA detectors together)

summary.plain: A 14,000-tonne block of plastic tubes filled with a liquid that flashes when particles pass through, sitting on the surface in northern Minnesota. It catches the few neutrinos that survive an 810-kilometre trip from Chicago.
summary.technical: 14 kt totally-active segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with mineral-oil-based liquid scintillator, 15.5 x 15.5 x 59.8 m, on the surface at Ash River 810 km from the NuMI target and 14.6 mrad off axis.

technology.quote: Charged particle tracking is accomplished via PVC cells filled with a mineral oil-based liquid scintillator.
technology.value: segmented tracking calorimeter of extruded PVC cells filled with liquid scintillator, read out by avalanche photodiodes
